first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly on the iPad. The opening tells me straight away how it works, backwards from the ceremony, with a real example time. Sensible and plain. I'm not the one in the main chair, though, so I kept looking for where I, and her grandmother, fit into the morning.

journey.quote: For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one.
journey.reaction: Good, a real example rather than waffle. But what on earth is a 'first look'? Nobody had one at my wedding. I had to read on to half-work it out.

journey.section: How a wedding morning timeline works
journey.quote: From where you dress to where you marry, allowing for a slow lift or a long walk.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Someone has thought about lifts and walking. That's exactly the sort of thing I worry about with Mum.

journey.section: The order of the hair and makeup chairs
journey.quote: Start with anyone who has to leave early, anyone with the simplest look, and anyone whose hair needs time to set. Children sit mid-morning, once fed and settled.
journey.reaction: Children get a mention but the mothers don't. I'll want my hair done, and so will her grandmother. Are we in this schedule or not? Nobody wants to discover at 9am that there's no chair for the mother of the bride.

journey.section: How long bridal hair and makeup takes
journey.quote: Get their figures in writing and build the morning on them.
journey.reaction: Now that's what I like to hear. In writing. I'd say the same to my daughter.

journey.section: A sample wedding morning timeline for a 4pm ceremony
journey.quote: 3.15pm. Any family photos you are happy to take before the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Fine, but then everyone stands about until 4pm. My mother can't be on her feet in the sun for the best part of an hour. A word about older relatives here would show me you'd thought of them.

journey.section: When the ceremony is in the morning
journey.quote: Move the ceremony to 11am with the same people and team, and that chair moves to 4.30am.
journey.reaction: Good grief. But at least it's honest, and it explains why an earlier ceremony costs you a lie-in. Useful to show my husband.

journey.quote: How long is the walk or drive, and does it involve stairs, sand or a slope in a long gown?
journey.reaction: Right question, but only thinking of the bride in the gown. My question is whether Mum with her walking frame can get there too.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person.
journey.reaction: One person, accountable, including payments. That's what I'm paying half for. I'd still want to know their name and whether I can ring them.

journey.section: Plan the morning with one person
journey.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing before any work, and in our time zone. That answers half my worries in one sentence. This is the line I'd forward to my husband.

unanswered_questions: Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the morning itself, at a venue overseas?
Is the 'conversation' with Wedded Concierge a phone call with a real person, or a form?
How are deposits paid to overseas suppliers protected, and are quotes in AUD?
Where do the mother of the bride and grandmother fit in the hair and makeup schedule?
Can older guests with a walking frame get from the suite to the ceremony site, and is there somewhere shaded to sit while waiting?

turn_offs_found.quote: 2pm. First look, then couple portraits close to where you are getting ready.
turn_offs_found.why: 'First look' is used all through the article and never explained. Not slang exactly, but it makes me feel out of touch, which is the last thing I want from a page my daughter sent me.

would_share_with: My husband, with the sentence about the fee in writing underlined
My daughter, to ask whether Mum and I are counted in the chairs

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It's the most reassuring line on the page. I'd click if I knew it led to a phone call with a person, not just an online form. And really it's my daughter's decision to make the first enquiry; I'd be telling her to.

top_3_changes: Count mothers and grandmothers in the chair order, so the parents can see they are part of the schedule.
Explain 'first look' the first time it appears.
Mention older relatives and mobility in the destination questions and the family photos slot, not only the bride in her gown.

suggested_edits.old: Start with anyone who has to leave early, anyone with the simplest look, and anyone whose hair needs time to set. Children sit mid-morning, once fed and settled.
suggested_edits.new: Start with anyone who has to leave early, anyone with the simplest look, and anyone whose hair needs time to set. Children sit mid-morning, once fed and settled. If mothers or grandmothers are having their hair or makeup done, give them a chair and a row on the schedule too.
suggested_edits.reason: Parents are part of the morning and want to see they are counted.

suggested_edits.old: 3. **Photos before the ceremony.** Portraits with a first look, or getting-ready photos only without one.
suggested_edits.new: 3. **Photos before the ceremony.** Portraits with a first look (when the couple see each other privately before the ceremony), or getting-ready photos only without one.
suggested_edits.reason: The term is used throughout and never defined.

suggested_edits.old: - **Distance to the ceremony site.** How long is the walk or drive, and does it involve stairs, sand or a slope in a long gown?
suggested_edits.new: - **Distance to the ceremony site.** How long is the walk or drive, and does it involve stairs, sand or a slope in a long gown? Can older relatives, or anyone with a walking frame, make the same trip, and is there a seat in the shade while they wait?
suggested_edits.reason: Mobility of older guests is a core worry for the paying parent; this adds a question, not a claim.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret, funding parent
No invented brand facts; gaps listed as unanswered questions
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, durations as fact, fees, vendors, on-ground staff, transfers, availability or Advisor running the morning
HTML comments and VERIFY markers treated as invisible

open_questions.question: Can the CTA say what the first step with Wedded Concierge is (for example a call), if the brand confirms that? Not added in edits because it is not stated in the draft.

assumptions: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated, so weight reactions accordingly.
Margaret arrives via a link from her daughter and reads top to bottom on an iPad.
